claim_scope: Let X be an equidimensional variety of dimension d over a field, with a chosen rational point a. Let R partition a finite index set I, with the empty set explicitly included as one block, and choose J in R. In Z_(R,J) impose equal coordinates on each block and x_i=a for i in J. Then Z_(R,J) is canonically a product of m copies of X, where m=|R|−1−1_(J≠empty). In particular J=empty gives dimension (|R|−1)d. The empty block contributes no coordinate.

Let f:X→S be proper, with X regular of pure dimension D+1, and smooth except at a single ordinary quadratic point of the special fibre. For rational ell-adic coefficients with ell≠p, the local vanishing-cycle space is a line in relative middle degree D. Inertia acts on that line by the nontrivial quadratic character when D is even, and trivially when D is odd. The regular-total-space hypothesis is essential for this conclusion; an even ramified base change can kill the character and leave a singular total space.

claim_scope: Over C let C0 be the affine cone of the quadratic equation sum(z_i²)=0, and let U={sum(z_i²)=1} have complex dimension D≥1. A shifted vanishing-cycle comparison must retain the degree-zero specialization map or use reduced cohomology; an unmodified all-degree identification that discards H⁰ is false. claim_scope: In the essential Euclidean reflection representation of a finite real reflection group, let alpha_i be inward unit simple normals and let G be their positive-definite Gram matrix, with G_ij=−cos(pi/m_ij) for i≠j. The dual simple vectors have Gram matrix G^(−1); their normalized cosine is (G^(−1))_ij divided by sqrt((G^(−1))_ii(G^(−1))_jj). Every entry of G^(−1) is nonnegative, so two vectors in the same closed essential chamber have nonnegative scalar product. No equality of those dual cosines with cos(pi/m_ij) is asserted.

claim_scope: Let S be connected and locally noetherian, with ell invertible, and interpret the source special-weight-zero class as Q_ell-subquotients of R⁰g_*Q_ell for smooth projective morphisms of relative dimension zero, allowing finite sums. A lisse Q_ell-sheaf belongs to this class if and only if its monodromy image is finite. Any finite-monodromy representation is a summand of finitely many copies of a finite-group regular representation, realized by a finite étale cover. Arbitrary lisse Q_ell-sheaves need not have finite monodromy.

claim_scope: Let V be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and H an additive subgroup, such as the proposed integral Hom group. If there are an integer N≥1 and a finitely generated Z-lattice L in V with H contained in N^(−1)L, then H is a finitely generated Z-module. claim_scope: Let X be a smooth separated complex algebraic variety of dimension n and let g:Y→X be smooth projective of relative dimension j≥0. Let F be a rational direct summand of R^j g_*Q and assume the compatible relative Lefschetz splitting realizes H^i(X,F) as a direct summand of H^(i+j)(Y,Q) in mixed Hodge structures. Then its Hodge level is at most min(i+j,2n−i+j), with vanishing outside the possible cohomological range. This is a numerical Hodge-level bound under the stated realization/splitting hypotheses; it does not establish the manuscript geometric motivic level for arbitrary admissible coefficients or singular X.

claim_scope: For a bounded convergent cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category, the induced filtration on H^n has associated graded pieces E_infinity^(p,n−p), and each such term is a subquotient of E_2^(p,n−p). Identifying a whole E_2 term with the abutment piece requires the relevant later differentials to vanish, as well as any compatibility needed to call that piece a specified weight piece. In the local double-blowup example the nonzero E_2^(0,2) is killed, so only a possible contribution through a subquotient survives as the defensible general formulation.

claim_scope: Over a finite field F_q with ell different from its characteristic, use the late untwisted dimension-type convention: type≤d is generated under finite sums, subquotients and extensions by untwisted cohomology of smooth projective varieties of dimension≤d. For r≥1, Q_ell(−r) has minimal type exactly r. It occurs as (R^r j_*Q_ell)_0 for j:G_m^r→A^r, and as H^(2r)(P^r,Q_ell). Thus the strict r−1 bound in this test cannot hold. This conclusion gives no general ordinary-direct-image theorem from the separate compact-support bound, and it does not concern the earlier Tate-stable D filtration.
